motion.name: chase-pulse
motion.value: 0.6 traverses/s of sim time; phase = (t x speed) mod 1, pure sim clock
motion.purpose: The linked cord's amber chase light, red end to blue end. Slowed x0.5 under prefers-reduced-motion, never removed — the pulse IS the linked signal.

motion.name: grace-dim
motion.value: linear opacity ramp to the 0.22 floor over the ~3 s grace window
motion.purpose: The popped cord's visible countdown; composes multiplicatively with the vanish fade so expiry never flashes back to full.

motion.name: grace-blink
motion.value: 3 Hz stepping up to 5 Hz at the window's half, 65% duty, final 1.5 s (the grace window's last half); keys on the sim clock
motion.purpose: The popped jack's band as a dying low-battery LED — blinking through half its window and quickening toward expiry (REFINE-1). Steady under reduced motion; the dim stays (state, not motion).

motion.name: deny-fade
motion.purpose: The flat red soft-cap deny ring on a rejected cube face — a mark, not a lamp.

motion.name: shatter-physics
motion.value: ballistic 9.81, restitutions 0.4 then 0.22, slide friction 9/s, 0.55 s lifetime, scale-out over the final 35% — 18 shards, base 0.03, scaled 0.75–1.8 (REFINE-1 legibility bump, was 14 at 0.02)
motion.purpose: The vanish shatter: deterministic seeded shards (dark steel + the failing end's band color), zero glow. Skipped entirely under reduced motion; the despawn/fade sequence is unchanged.

motion.name: dom-state
motion.value: instant — zero CSS transitions, zero keyframes, zero tweens
motion.purpose: DOM states flip the frame the sim state flips; hardware does not ease.

motion.name: dangle-settle
motion.value: sim-owned: dangle settles ~1.5 s without jitter; brush perturbation dampened x0.5 under reduced motion
motion.purpose: The feel layer — every moving pixel in the scene is the fixed-timestep solver, never an animation.

overview: Cords is staged as an early-80s hardware instrument faceplate brought to life: a charcoal steel bench under one warm lamp, machined panel seams falling into fog, eight steel modules each carrying a single candy color zone, and the hero object — real 1/4-inch phone plugs on dark rubber cords — lying across it. The interface recedes to a silkscreen faceplate strip along the bottom edge: tracked small-caps legends, squared segmented meters, machined keycap buttons. Nothing is costume; every printed word names a real state, and every lit pixel is live state.

The system's core honesty is the lit = live state only contract. The scene is unlit hardware — matte rubber, brushed steel, painted silkscreen — until the simulation says otherwise: a completed link's amber chase pulse traveling the cord, a meter row filling one segment per live cord, a popped jack's band blinking like a dying battery. Failure performs in the same hardware grammar: the jack shatters into dark steel shards plus one shard of its own color band, the cord dims through its grace countdown, and the meters count it down to zero.

Motion is sim-driven, never scripted — no CSS keyframes and no tweens anywhere. Every animated read is a pure function of the simulation's own clock and state, so the same sim instant always paints the same picture and a frozen sim holds its light still.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal steel ground — dark, never black; the bench reads as lit steel under the warm key.
Eight candy color zones, each doubling as a state ink (amber = live cords, jade = links, red/blue = plug polarity).
Silkscreen legends: tracked caps that name real state only; if the sim can't say it, the panel doesn't print it.
One glow budget: the chase-pulse amber on linked cords and the lit meter segments — nothing else glows, ever.
Machined depth: 1px bevels, seams, screws, and one warm key light; flat surfaces, no glass, no gradients.
Sim-clock motion: deterministic, headless-testable, no keyframes; reduced motion slows or holds effects, never removes live-state meaning.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow exists only where live state lives: the chase-pulse amber on a linked cord, the lit meter segments, and the focus bracket. Everything else is painted, machined, or lit by the key — never emissive. A decorative glow is a bug.

rules.name: The State-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every saturated color names a live state: amber = cords alive, jade = links, red/blue = plug polarity, candy zones = module identities. Saturated color is never used for mood, section, or filler.

rules.name: The Silkscreen Honesty Rule
rules.body: Every printed string names a real state or a real control. Labels never become costume; the empty-scene hint disappears the moment one cord exists, and the meters are aria-hidden because the live-region summary already speaks the counts.

rules.name: The Machined-Edge Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat; depth is machined (inset bevels, seams, screws) or lit (the key, the fog). No drop shadows, no glass, no gradients, no blur.

dos: Do light a pixel only when the sim justifies it: lit segments = live counts, chase pulse = linked, band lift = seated-and-linked, band blink = dying.
Do print only real state in silkscreen grammar: tracked caps (0.14-0.34em), Legend/Dim inks, mono numerals for every number.
Do compose new panel modules from the strip's furniture: #0d0f12 module seam + 24px padding-left, squared slots, 2px keycaps, screw fasteners.
Do keep candy color tied to state or module identity, each with its darker keyline.
Do drive every animated read from the sim clock; reuse the purity seam (pure function of sim state + sim time).
Do honor the reduced-motion seams exactly: slow the pulse x0.5, hold the blink steady, skip particles, keep the dim.
donts: Don't add decorative glow, bloom, halos, additive blending, or any emissive material outside the chase pulse and lit meter segments.
Don't use drop shadows, glass, blur, or gradients — depth is machined or lit.
Don't print a label, hint, or number the sim cannot back with live state; don't show the empty hint while a cord exists.
Don't animate with CSS transitions/keyframes, wall-clock tweens, or Math.random().
Don't let red mean anything but input polarity / denial, or recolor the stretch ticks — measurement furniture is neutral ink.
Don't introduce display type or sentence case on the panel; the voice is all-caps silkscreen at 9-15px with tabular mono numerals.
